motivation.problems: Platform engineers in this catalog restructure infrastructure code that is already running. The most common task is a flat Terraform root module that has to become local modules with for_each keys, for example terraform-arcgis-enterprise-module-refactor, terraform-shortly-production-module-refactor and terraform-armada-ecs-module-refactor. The change must reach production as address moves only, because the team cannot plan against a live account. A second pattern is replacing positional count with stable keys for zones, services or stages, as in terraform-froggy-adserver-api-module-refactor, where operations were indexed in several historical orders. A third is extracting reusable components from an app that builds everything inline, as in cdk-skytrail-platform-ts-componentize, where synthesized output must not change. The showcase set adds two further problems: moving a stack between tools while a preview stays clean (the Pulumi ports) and bringing a stack under a policy pack without replacing resources (policy-waivers-example).
motivation.how_tasks_exemplify: Each task ships a copy of the stack with its recorded production state or recorded templates, an offline toolchain and no network. The Terraform refactor tasks include a CI script that plans with refresh disabled and runs conftest on the plan. The instruction states module ownership, key rules, root variables with today's defaults and outputs. A separate verifier container holds its own pristine state, plans the agent's configuration, and then plans hidden changes such as an added key under a fresh name, a removed key or a changed entry. The CDK task compares synthesized templates for hidden configurations. The Pulumi tasks run previews against an imported stack and against a copy with swapped generated IDs. Most tasks score zero when a gate fails.
prompt_patterns: A refactor request for a named production stack that lists target modules, ownership, key rules, root variables and outputs, and requires a plan of moves only (terraform-earthobs-stac-module-refactor).
A componentization request that lists every construct class with its path, props and public properties, and requires identical synthesized templates (cdk-accelerator-platform-ts-componentize).
A migration brief for an imported stack with an empty program, with naming, config and equivalence rules and banned options (pulumi-cats-vs-dogs-ts-migration).
A compliance remediation request with numbered requirements, a policy pack, a guardrail spec and an exceptions register, graded with hidden variable probes (policy-waivers-example).
A bulleted list of needs followed by constraints to keep working, such as a clean preview and unchanged owned files (pulumi-atlasgrid-ecs-ts-migration).
open_questions: The tasks file contains 29 Terraform module refactors and one CDK task. Pulumi ports and policy remediation appear only in the showcase set, so their share of the 325 tasks is UNKNOWN.
policy-waivers-example sits in the SRE-xai-ots batch and the other Terraform tasks in IaC-ots. The files do not say how the two batches differ in origin or authoring.
Seniority labels in the input (all Senior) are not stated in any task file, so their source is UNKNOWN.

The README files and instructions name real open-source projects and companies as the origin of some stacks, but task.toml leaves source_repository empty. Whether these stacks are derived from public repositories is UNKNOWN.

The Terraform tasks say a pristine state exists in the verifier, but the grader and spec were only skimmed for the Terraform tasks. Details of the hidden probes for the Terraform refactors beyond what instruction.md states were not reviewed.
Reference solutions and the full grade.py logic were deliberately not described, so the catalog owner should confirm how much of the grading detail may be published.
Show folders outside the showcase list, such as terraform-csyeapp-production-policy-remediation, were not read.

tasks.workflow: A cloud security engineer owns the change that brings a production stack and its exceptions register into line with a policy pack after a quarterly review. Findings that can be fixed in place must be fixed, and only findings that need a resource replacement may be waived in the register. Every production resource must stay at its address and be updated in place, and the fixes must still hold when the team adds, removes or retunes collection entries.
tasks.prompt_pattern: A compliance remediation request that points to a policy pack, a deploy-stage guardrail spec and an exceptions register, and lists numbered requirements covering in-place-only updates, allowed new resource types and hidden generality probes.

tasks.name: terraform-csyeapp-production-policy-remediation
tasks.environment_mermaid:
flowchart LR
  A["debian bookworm slim agent container, no network"] --> B["terraform 1.16.4 and conftest 0.70.1 on the path"]
  A --> C["AWS provider 5.100.0 from a local mirror"]
  A --> D["Stack in /workspace/infra with recorded terraform.tfstate"]
  D --> E["OPA policy pack in policies with README"]
  D --> F["scripts/ci-plan.sh: init, validate, plan, conftest"]

  B --> H
  D --> H
  E --> H
  H --> I["Edited /workspace/infra collected as artifact"]
  I --> J["Separate verifier with pristine state and its own policy pack"]

environment_facts: Base image debian:bookworm-slim pinned by digest with Terraform 1.16.4, conftest 0.70.1, git, jq, python3 and tmux; the AWS provider 5.100.0 and archive provider are installed in a local mirror (environment/Dockerfile).
The stack is copied to /workspace/infra, committed to a git repository and initialized offline, with proxy variables pointing at a dead address (environment/Dockerfile).
scripts/ci-plan.sh runs init, validate, a refresh-free plan against the recorded state, and conftest with all namespaces over policies/ (tests/trusted/scripts/ci-plan.sh).
The policy pack is a set of Rego rules documented per rule id in policies/README.md, covering EC2, Lambda, DynamoDB, RDS and IAM, among others (environment/infra/policies/README.md).
The grader plans against its own pristine state and policy pack and runs 12 probe var files in tests/probes (tests/spec.json, task.toml).

tasks.workflow: A cloud security engineer owns the production infrastructure code for a web application and finds CI red because the platform policy pack rejects the plan, although the plan against the recorded state is clean. The engineer has to remediate the logging, least-privilege and cost rules while keeping every recorded resource at its address, touching only an allowlist of arguments, and keeping the fixes valid when channels, buckets, tags or retention inputs change.
tasks.prompt_pattern: A CI-failure ticket with a bulleted change allowlist, retention and ownership rules, a keep-working list and offline setup notes, and no list of the failing policy rules.
